note: Machine-readable twin of reference/skill-map.md. skills.ts resolves a job kind to the skills that should be loaded before work starts. `prefer` is loaded first and owns the job; `also` is loaded only when its trigger applies; `external` is not installed locally and must be fetched. Nothing here is vendored into the factory — these are references. If a skill is installed, use it; if not, offer the install line; if it cannot be installed, follow its `degrade` note and say out loud that you are on the degraded path.

registry._comment: Provenance for every skill this map routes to. `source` is recorded ONLY where it is actually known — a guessed repo URL is worse than none, because it sends the user somewhere that does not exist. Where the source is unknown, `find` says how to locate it and `degrade` says what to do without it.

impeccable.source: npm package `impeccable` — the skill drives itself through `npx impeccable`
impeccable.degrade: Do the interface work inline against a written craft floor: commit to one visual world before editing, inspect the incumbent tokens/theme first, ban gradient-text and unearned glassmorphism, and verify on desktop and mobile in one batched pass rather than an open-ended polish loop.

find-docs.source: https://github.com/upstash/context7 — the skill is a wrapper over the Context7 CLI
find-docs.install: npx ctx7@latest library "<name>" then npx ctx7@latest docs <id> "<question>"
find-docs.degrade: Call the Context7 CLI directly — it needs no skill wrapper. Only fall back to WebSearch when the library is absent from Context7, and never answer API questions from memory: training data lags releases and a wrong signature costs a debugging cycle.

superpowers.degrade: The discipline it carries is already restated in the Laws and in reference/verify.md. Install it for the full playbooks; do not reimplement it.

handoff.degrade: Write the handoff by hand against the fixed schema in reference/context-discipline.md.

code-review.degrade: Dispatch a subagent whose only instruction is to refute the diff.

security-review.degrade: Review auth, secrets, input handling and network boundaries by hand against the diff.

simplify.degrade: Run `slop.ts check` and consolidate what it names.

run.degrade: Start the app yourself and capture the output as evidence.

dataviz.degrade: Pick one chart form per question, label axes, and keep the palette to one accent.

loop.degrade: Drive the loop from reference/loop.md with an explicit stop condition.

schedule.degrade: Ask the user to run the loop manually, or generate a cron/GitHub Actions workflow.

artifact-design.degrade: Write the deliverable as a plain markdown file and hand over the path.

artifact-diagramming.degrade: Use a Mermaid fenced block — it renders in markdown and in published artifacts with no external library. Draw the mechanism, not the box-and-arrow restatement of the headings.

registry._provenance_warning: The community design/motion skills below circulate as copies. A GitHub search for any of their names returns many mirrors and forks with no single authoritative upstream, and the skill files themselves record no source. So each entry gives a SEARCH that will find current copies rather than a URL that might point at an abandoned fork. Verify what you find before installing it: read its SKILL.md, and never run an install command from a repo you have not opened.

design-taste-frontend.degrade: Audit before redesigning: read the incumbent tokens and one real page, name what is templated about it, then commit to a single direction and apply it consistently. The value it adds is refusing the default centred-hero-three-cards layout.

emil-design-eng.find: gh search repos emil-design-eng  — often bundled with impeccable and design-taste-frontend
emil-design-eng.degrade: Work at component level: hit states, focus rings, disabled states, loading and empty states, and transitions under 200ms. The details it owns are the ones no detector catches.

apple-design.degrade: Follow Apple's Human Interface Guidelines directly for gesture, spring and material questions; prefer interruptible spring animations over fixed-duration easing, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.

pick-ui-library.degrade: Choose from what the project already depends on; introduce a new component library only when the user asks, and say what it costs in bundle size.

redesign-existing-projects.degrade: Audit first, list what is generic, then change one layer at a time — tokens, then layout, then components — verifying the app still runs between layers.

high-end-visual-design.degrade: Spend the budget on type scale, spacing rhythm and one confident accent; avoid the tells — gradient text, unearned glassmorphism, evenly-weighted card grids.

imagegen-frontend-web.degrade: Generate one reference image per section rather than a single compressed board, and keep one palette across all of them.

imagegen-frontend-mobile.degrade: Design per screen with a consistent nav shell, and keep body text at a size that survives a phone mockup.

image-to-code.find: gh search repos image-to-code skill claude
image-to-code.degrade: Generate the target image first, analyse it explicitly in writing, then implement against that written analysis rather than against a memory of the picture.

brandkit.find: gh search repos brandkit skill claude
brandkit.degrade: Produce a one-page system: logo lockup, palette with hex values and roles, type pairing with scale, and three applied mockups.

fal-design.find: https://fal.ai — the skill wraps the fal.ai API; needs FAL_KEY
fal-design.degrade: Ask the user which image or video service they have a key for; do not generate assets without an explicit key and a stated per-job price.

improve-animations.degrade: Audit existing motion for duration, easing and purpose; anything over 400ms or without a reason to exist is a finding.

find-animation-opportunities.degrade: Look for state changes the user cannot see happen — list appends, route changes, async completion — and propose motion only there.

review-animations.degrade: Review the motion diff for reduced-motion handling, layout thrash and interruptibility.

animation-vocabulary.degrade: Ask the user to describe the effect and name it yourself before building it — an unnamed effect gets rebuilt three times.

scroll-world.degrade: A scroll cinematic needs pre-rendered frames and a scrub engine; without the skill, say so and scope it explicitly rather than approximating with CSS.

code-structure.find: gh search repos code-structure skill claude
code-structure.degrade: Apply the deep-module vocabulary in reference/program-design.md; extract a shared module only at the second real caller.

full-output-enforcement.degrade: Law 2 and Law 4 already carry this: no truncation, no placeholders, and a token limit means a handoff rather than an abridged file.

obsidian-memory.find: user-specific — this one is wired to a private CouchDB/Obsidian vault
obsidian-memory.degrade: Durable facts go to FACTORY.md and the ledger instead. Do not attempt to reach a memory backend that is not configured.

searxng-search-internet.find: https://github.com/searxng/searxng for the engine; the skill wraps a user-hosted instance
searxng-search-internet.degrade: Use the built-in WebSearch and WebFetch tools.

kole-kimi.find: user-specific — routes work to Kimi K3 through a local CLIProxyAPI gateway
kole-kimi.degrade: Do the work yourself. Never route work to a gateway that is not configured.

omniroute-router.find: user-specific — an OmniRoute gateway must be running
omniroute-router.degrade: Do the work yourself rather than routing to an unavailable gateway.

drawio-skill.find: gh search repos drawio skill claude  — requires the draw.io desktop CLI
drawio-skill.degrade: Write the diagram as Mermaid in the artifact; it renders in markdown and in published artifacts without any external binary.

agent-browser.install: npm i -g agent-browser  (or brew install agent-browser), then `agent-browser install`
agent-browser.degrade: Use Playwright or the chrome-devtools CLI directly. Whatever you use, capture the artefact — a screenshot or a recording — and treat the artefact as evidence only after checking it came from a real environment.

gpt-taste.degrade: Covered by impeccable and design-taste-frontend; skip it rather than substituting.

stitch-design-taste.degrade: Write the DESIGN.md by hand: type scale, palette with roles, spacing scale, motion defaults.

minimalist-ui.degrade: One accent colour, generous spacing, no shadows deeper than a hairline border.

industrial-brutalist-ui.degrade: Rigid grid, extreme type-scale contrast, utilitarian palette — commit fully or not at all; half-brutalism reads as broken.

framer-expert.find: https://www.framer.com — the skill drives the Framer MCP plugin
framer-expert.degrade: Framer work needs the MCP connection or an API key; say so rather than producing code that cannot be applied.

framerapi.find: https://www.framer.com — headless writes need a Framer API key
framerapi.degrade: Same as framer-expert: stop and tell the user what credential is missing.

triggers.find-docs: any named library, framework, SDK, CLI or cloud service is involved
triggers.obsidian-memory: the project has prior history in shared memory
triggers.searxng-search-internet: the answer is outside the codebase and outside library docs

triggers.obsidian-memory: prior product decisions may already be recorded

triggers.code-structure: operational logic is duplicated across flows, or you are deciding what belongs in shared services
triggers.drawio-skill: the architecture has 3+ components and a diagram would carry it better than prose

triggers.code-structure: the design touches shared services or repeated operational blocks

triggers.full-output-enforcement: always — it is the anti-truncation contract
triggers.find-docs: any library API is being called
triggers.kole-kimi: the user has asked to delegate grunt work to Kimi
triggers.omniroute-router: the work is bulk and routine and quota matters

triggers.run: the change needs to be seen working in the real app, not just in tests
triggers.code-review: a diff exists and correctness review is due
triggers.security-review: the change touches auth, secrets, input handling, or network boundaries

triggers.simplify: the diff works but carries duplication or over-abstraction
triggers.security-review: the change touches auth, secrets, input handling, or network boundaries

triggers.find-docs: the failure is inside a third-party library's behavior
triggers.run: the bug must be reproduced in the running app

triggers.impeccable: always for interface work — it owns the craft floor and the command set
triggers.design-taste-frontend: landing page, portfolio or marketing site that must not read as templated
triggers.emil-design-eng: component-level polish, micro-interactions and the invisible details
triggers.pick-ui-library: the component library has not been chosen yet
triggers.redesign-existing-projects: an existing site is being upgraded rather than built

triggers.imagegen-frontend-web: web design references are needed before code
triggers.imagegen-frontend-mobile: mobile app screens are being designed
triggers.image-to-code: a visual target must be generated first, then implemented to match
triggers.brandkit: brand guidelines, logo system or identity board
triggers.fal-design: images, video, logos or art direction must actually be generated
triggers.high-end-visual-design: the output must read as agency-grade rather than default

triggers.improve-animations: existing motion needs an audit and a roadmap
triggers.find-animation-opportunities: the UI is static and should not be
triggers.animation-vocabulary: the user described an effect without naming it
triggers.apple-design: the motion should feel physical — springs, gestures, momentum, interruptible transitions
triggers.scroll-world: a scroll-scrubbed cinematic landing is wanted

triggers.searxng-search-internet: positioning needs real competitor and market evidence
triggers.brandkit: the work is identity-level, not campaign-level
triggers.imagegen-frontend-web: the deliverable is a landing page concept
triggers.fal-design: ad creative or campaign imagery must be produced

triggers.artifact-design: the deliverable is a page a human will read and share
triggers.artifact-diagramming: a diagram carries the mechanism better than prose
triggers.drawio-skill: the diagram must be editable or exported

triggers.loop: the user wants iteration on a wall-clock interval in this session
triggers.schedule: the loop should survive this session and run in the cloud

triggers.handoff: compacting this session into a document another session can pick up
triggers.obsidian-memory: the fact is durable and belongs in shared memory, not just this project

humanlayer-codebase-design.what: Deep-module design vocabulary: module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality. Plus the deletion test and design-it-twice.
humanlayer-codebase-design.why: This is the vocabulary the program-design layer is written in. Without it the layer degenerates into restating the architecture.

humanlayer-improve-codebase-architecture.what: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, report them, then work through one.

humanlayer-show-me.what: Explain the current topic visually — diagrams, code-shape sketches, focused HTML.

humanlayer-design-control-loop.what: Interview-driven design of an agentic control loop: sensor, controller, actuator, disturbances.

humanlayer-build-iterated-agentic-loop.what: Build a repo-local skill plus a scheduled coding-agent workflow with a memory file that carries feedback between runs.

humanlayer-improve-claude-md.what: Rewrite CLAUDE.md using <important if> blocks so instructions actually get followed.

superpowers.what: The 14-skill agentic development methodology: brainstorming, writing-plans, executing-plans, subagent-driven-development, dispatching-parallel-agents, verification-before-completion, test-driven-development, systematic-debugging, requesting/receiving-code-review, git worktrees, writing-skills.
superpowers.why: The factory's discipline layer is derived from these. Install the plugin to get the full playbooks rather than the summaries embedded here.

superpowers-systematic-debugging.what: Root-cause-first debugging discipline: no fix proposed before the mechanism is understood.
